_comment: Build record for the Debian-host gateway.
RETARGETED 2026-08-29. This manifest described `symon-gateway` at 41b9eda8... for three
days after the 2026-08-26 cutover promoted `symoneural-gateway` at 61f8df5b... and made it
the binary the unit launches. The old binary is still on disk, so the manifest verified
cleanly against it and nothing noticed -- a manifest can be internally consistent and still
describe an artifact that no longer serves. `regenerate.sh --check` now cross-checks the
recorded path against the unit's ExecStart for exactly that reason.
RESOLVED 2026-09-03, and the note is rewritten rather than deleted so the next reader can
see the dependency existed and how it closed. It said `ops/build-gateway.sh` still set
OUT=$SRC/target/release/symon-gateway, so any gateway build would re-stale this manifest,
and that the underlying half-completed rename also held apps/test_gateway_unit.py red.
Both halves are now closed: build-gateway.sh:80 derives OUT="$SRC/target/release/$BIN_NAME"
from Cargo.toml rather than hard-coding a name, so a build writes the binary this manifest
already describes; and apps/test_gateway_unit.py passes 9/9. Re-verified at HEAD 4c36b77f:
the sha256 below matches the on-disk artifact and the running process's /proc/PID/exe.
Toolchain fields are carried forward from the 2026-08-26 migration record, which names the
same rustc/cargo for that day's builds. `built_on` is NOT carried forward: the previous
value belonged to the 09:28 build of the OLD binary, and this artifact's build time was
never recorded. `file_mtime` is an observation, not a build timestamp.

superseded_artifact.note: pre-cutover control, still on disk, no longer launched

source_reproducible: unverified -- no reproducibility experiment has been run for this artifact
